plain: To block or defeat someone's plan.

webster.text: To frustrate; to defeat; to render vain or nugatory, as an effort or attempt.

more.text: A blunt sword, or one that has a button at the end covered with leather; used in fencing.
Any thing of another color, or of different qualities, which serves to adorn, or set off another thing to advantage.

example.quote: I wish this government may answer the expectation of its friends, and foil the apprehension of its enemies.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 6, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
